slots._slotId: 🔴 `HBA`, RULED 2026-08-14 BY THE COORDINATOR, AND THE RULING IS FREE BECAUSE `serves` MADE IT COSMETIC. This read `SLOT-HBA-ALL` - an invented token, flagged as the only one in the file - back when the slot id was the ONLY join to a vector's `slot` field. It is not any more: `serves` carries the citable ids, so the slot id is now purely an internal key (the tag fragment, and a map-hash input) that no vector cites. `HBA` is what the DEPLOYED mirror uses - `ir/test-project001/HarnessMirror.ir` declares HX_HBA_Start, HX_HBA_V000..V019, HX_HBA_R000..R007 - so keeping it leaves 35 tag names unchanged, where the invented token would rename every one of them to express a grouping key that no longer addresses anything. Cost with no purchaser.
slots._serves: THE MANY-TO-ONE MAP. md:173-186 - the six ids are ONE SLOT'S SERIAL PHASES, not six slots: md:179-181 states all six drive the SAME instance, the SAME DB_Input.Test members and the SAME DB_Controls.FaultReset. The ids themselves are taken from the submission's own `slot` fields, which is the authority for its own ids. It needs no partition, which is part of why it is right: every served id addresses the same vector band, the same result band and the same start bool.
slots._servesRunInOrder: THE GROUP ORDER IS THE COORDINATOR'S SENTENCE AND NOT THIS FILE'S. Stated by ruling O-3, 2026-08-14: the five ORDINARY groups run RAISE, CLEAR, LATCH, RESET, PAIR - true document order, verified against conformance-vectors-b.json (first appearance: RAISE VB-HBA-001, CLEAR VB-HBA-005, LATCH VB-HBA-011, RESET VB-HBA-013, PAIR VB-HBA-024). Needed because the submission carries NO total order of its own: MEASURED, every group restarts `index` at 0, so 27 vectors carry only six distinct index values, and a merge without a major key gives one vector per group reading Results[0] while 21 of 27 packages carry another vector's run.
slots._boundarySpanning: 🔴 SLOT-HBA-STARTUP IS NOT IN THAT SEQUENCE, AND ITS POSITION IN `serves` ABOVE IS NOT READ. Ruling O-3, 2026-08-14, from the vectors' OWN fields rather than from a decision handed down: VB-HBA-019.._scenario reads `STARTUP - RIDES AN ALREADY-SCHEDULED DISRUPTIVE BOUNDARY (X-F) ... The boundary stops and restarts the CPU`, and its _observability reads `THE HARNESS IS DISCONNECTED ACROSS THE DOWNLOAD (D18) and nobody is polling while the first scan happens`. Those five vectors REQUIRE a CPU restart inside them. Run inline they would execute with no restart, and PAIR would then run after a restart nobody sequenced, against a freshly cleared accumulator and a reconnected harness - a confident wrong answer that reads as a clean pass. A run carrying them is refused BY NAME (LoopOutcome.NotSchedulable). EXPLICITLY UNRUNNABLE BEATS IMPLICITLY MIS-RUN.

slots._resultSourceOrder: 🔴 ORDER CORRECTED 2026-08-14, AND THE DIVERGENCE IT CLOSES WAS SILENT. This list was in md:73-80 order (Armed, ScenarioDone, Alarm, StopReq); the DEPLOYED layer is in the order below (Alarm, StopReq, Armed, ScenarioDone) - `ir/test-project001/FC_HarnessCopyLayer.ir:41-44` and `wire-prediction.md` section 1, registers 27/28/29/30. MEASURED by generating from this file and diffing against the committed IR: the tag TABLE came out identical, and the copy layer's result network had four signals in two different orders. Since the binding drives BOTH the emitted rungs AND the result decode (`SlotBinding.ResultRegisterOf`), the md order was internally consistent and would simply have moved four signals to different registers at the next deploy, with nothing to flag it - a re-deploy is exactly when a client mirror written against the old map goes quietly wrong. md's table is a NAME mapping and states no register order, so this is a transcription of the artifact, not a choice between two claims. The four violation latches were already in the deployed order (md:77-80 = registers 31-34) and are unmoved.

resultSources._latch: 🔴 THE LATCH, GRANTED 2026-08-14 BY THE COORDINATOR - AND IT IS A TRANSCRIPTION OF A REQUEST, NOT AN AUTHORSHIP. The trace has two halves and both are in artifacts that already exist. (1) THE SUBMISSION ASKS FOR IT IN WRITING: conformance-vectors-b.json `map._capabilityRequest` - `(a) Sampled and Latched on the two block outputs. (b) THE LATCHES MUST BE ARMED BY THE STIMULUS MODEL'S PHASE FLAG (HBA_Stim.Armed), not free-running from T=0`. (2) THE ARM SOURCE IS THE COORDINATOR'S OWN PROSE: md:73 - `HBA_Stim.Armed | .Stim.Armed | arms the copy layer's observation latches`, in those words. So this grants a capability the vector author requested, using the arm source the coordinator's prose names. WHY BOTH FLAGS: `transient` alone yields the once-per-WAVE latch, which sets on the first firing and stays set - index 2 would read identical to index 1 and a signal that never fired again would read as one that did. `rearmsEachIndex` makes it phase-armed off the slot's start bool, which the client already drives low before every index. WHY `armedBy` ON TOP: FB_HarnessViolationLatch's own block comment gives the reason - every run legitimately begins by driving the monitor through a clear-down, and a free-running latch would fill from that and read violated whatever the monitor did. COST: one register each, in the latch band AFTER the values, so no value offset moves. Results 8 -> 10, mirror 35 -> 37 - and MB_HOLD_REG is ALREADY `P#M1000.0 WORD 37` (FB_Comms_ModbusServer.ir:31).

_review._whatIsNowEnforcedThatWasNot: (a) An input NO BOUND TARGET CONSUMES is refused by name - it used to be dropped in silence, leaving the register at zero. (b) A cited value the encoding tables do not name is refused by name rather than given an invented code. (c) A many-to-one slot with no stated group order is refused - `index` alone is not a position, and a merge without a major key gives 21 of 27 packages another vector's run. (d) A BOUNDARY-SPANNING group is refused from an inline wave: SLOT-HBA-STARTUP's own vectors say the boundary stops and restarts the CPU and that the harness is disconnected across the download, so running them inline would be a confident wrong answer that reads as a clean pass.
_review._whatThisFileStillCannotSay: The program's RETENTIVE %M EXTENT. `MirrorGeometry` gives it no default deliberately - it is a property of the program, not of the CPU - and `harness-run` supplies 256 when the binding is silent. That number is an input to the MAP HASH and therefore to the BUILD STAMP, so the identity of a generated build rests on a value nobody has measured. It is printed on every generate-only run, labelled DEFAULTED, rather than refused: no party in this loop can measure it, and a gate nobody can satisfy blocks its own recovery path.
